issue.title: fix(dns): share in-flight lookups between concurrent requests

repository.name: undici
repository.description: An HTTP/1.1 client, written from scratch for Node.js

issue.body:
## This relates to...

Fixes #5974

## Rationale

When the DNS interceptor has no usable records for a hostname (cold cache, or every cached record has expired), each request starts its own `lookup()`. A burst of concurrent requests to the same host therefore produces a burst of identical lookups; the reproduction in #5974 sees 100 lookups for 100 concurrent requests.

## Changes

### Bug Fixes

- `lib/interceptor/dns.js`: `DNSInstance` keeps a per-hostname list of callbacks waiting on an in-flight lookup. Requests that arrive while a lookup for the same hostname is pending join it instead of starting another one. When the lookup completes the records are stored once and each waiting request still runs `pick()` with its own origin (so ports/protocols are preserved and round-robin keeps working). A failed lookup rejects every waiting request and the pending entry is removed, so the next request retries.
- Requests that pass per-request `dns` options (`opts.dns`) keep their own lookup, since they may resolve differently.
- `docs/docs/api/Interceptors.md`: one sentence describing the shared in-flight lookup.
- `test/interceptors/dns.js`: two regression tests — 20 concurrent requests share one lookup and a second batch uses the cache; 5 concurrent requests sharing a failed lookup all reject with `ENOTFOUND`, and the following request performs a fresh lookup.

### Features

N/A

### Breaking Changes and Deprecations

N/A

## Testing (Node.js v22.20.0, Linux)

- `node --test --test-name-pattern='#5974' test/interceptors/dns.js`: 2/2 pass with the fix; both fail on unmodified `main` (20 lookups instead of 1; not all requests rejected by the failed lookup).
- The standalone script from #5974: `{ coldCacheLookups: 1, warmCacheLookups: 0 }` with the fix, `{ coldCacheLookups: 100, warmCacheLookups: 0 }` on `main`.
- `node --test test/interceptors/dns.js`: of 37 tests, 33 pass (including the two new ones), 3 are skipped because IPv6 localhost is unavailable here, and 1 fails: `Should respect DNS origin hostname for SNI on TLS`, with `ERR_SSL_SSL/TLS_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE`; it fails the same way on unmodified `main`, and leaves the run hanging until my 600 s timeout. I'm relying on CI for that one.
- `node --test test/interceptors/origin-isolation.js test/interceptors/deduplicate.js`: 73/73 pass.
- `npx eslint lib/interceptor/dns.js test/interceptors/dns.js`: clean.

- [ ] Benchmarked (**optional**)
- [x] Documented
- [x] Review ready

AI assistance was used to help prepare and verify this change.

issue.title: fix(dns): deduplicate concurrent lookups for the same hostname

repository.name: undici
repository.description: An HTTP/1.1 client, written from scratch for Node.js

issue.body:
Fixes: #5974

### Description
Concurrent requests resolving the same hostname when the DNS cache was cold previously triggered separate, redundant lookups for each request.

This PR tracks in-flight lookups per hostname using an internal map in `DNSInstance`:
- Concurrent requests for the same hostname join the in-flight resolution queue instead of initiating duplicate lookup calls.
- Once resolution finishes, results are cached once in `storage`, and each waiting request independently selects an address using `pick()` (preserving round-robin distribution and family affinity).
- If the lookup fails, in-flight state is cleared, all waiting callers receive the error, and subsequent requests can retry.

### Tests
- Added unit test in `test/interceptors/dns.js` verifying that concurrent requests share a single DNS lookup and subsequent requests use the cached result.
- Added unit test verifying that lookup failures clear in-flight tracking and reject all waiting callers while allowing subsequent retries.

repository.name: undici
repository.description: An HTTP/1.1 client, written from scratch for Node.js

issue.body:
## This relates to...

Fixes #5974

## Rationale

When several requests for the same hostname arrive before its DNS entry is cached, each one started its own lookup. A burst of concurrent requests to a cold hostname therefore triggered one resolver lookup per request instead of one for the group.

## Changes

`runLookup` now records an in-flight lookup in a `#pendingLookups` map keyed by the hostname plus the resolution-affecting options (`affinity`, `dualStack`). A request that finds a pending entry for its key is added to that entry's waiter list instead of starting a lookup of its own; otherwise it starts one and registers itself as the first waiter. When the lookup completes, every waiter runs the existing `pick` logic against the shared records, so each request still selects its own address and the per-request origin, port, protocol, and round-robin behavior are unchanged. The pending entry is removed before the result is fanned out, so a failed lookup is reported to all attached waiters and a later request for the same hostname starts a fresh lookup.

A regression test in `test/issue-5974.js` covers a cold-cache burst performing a single lookup (and a warm burst performing none), concurrent waiters picking addresses independently from the shared lookup, and a failing lookup being shared while its pending state is cleared so the next request retries. `npm run lint`, `npm run test:interceptors` (446 pass / 0 fail) and `npm run test:unit` (1613 pass / 0 fail) pass.

### Features

N/A

### Bug Fixes

- Concurrent requests for the same cold hostname now share a single DNS lookup instead of each starting their own. (Fixes #5974)

### Breaking Changes and Deprecations

N/A
